evidence.note: Correctness broke after first vectorization; agent diagnosed the simulator's read-all-then-write semantics and the RAW/WAR packing constraint, corrected its model of the machine rather than patching blindly.
Profiled engine utilization, found load engine idle at ~1/bundle, diagnosed the root cause (gather-address dependency), and fixed it — evidence-driven correction dropping 4234→2412.
WAR soft-dependency experiments produced 'No change'; agent recognized the assumption was wrong ('WAR was not the bottleneck') and stopped pursuing it instead of entrenching.
Explicitly compared falsified predictions to actual results (mux saved 53 cy vs estimated 235), revising the cost model to attribute the shortfall to load-idle waste in reset/mux rounds.
d=2 mux (1968) and d=3 mux (2020) each made cycles WORSE; agent diagnosed serial mul_add dependency chains and cleanly reverted to the 1945 known-good state each time.
Scratch-reuse (ip_/vp_) broke correctness; agent traced instruction-level addresses to find the wrong vload pointer, then reverted to 1956 — clean recovery preserving correct state.
Sustained persistence on the mux strategy despite repeated failures to close the gap; never decisively pivots to a fundamentally different approach, keeping it below the top anchor.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly treats falsified predictions as signals to revise its cost model (steps 54, 76, 133), reverts cleanly to known-good cycle counts after every broken or unhelpful change (steps 55, 113, 128, 164), and diagnoses WHY expectations were wrong via engine-utilization profiling — matching the level-8 description of clean reverts plus model revision without sunk-cost entrenchment on individual transforms. It falls short of 10 because, while individual transforms are handled well, the agent circles the same mux-based load-reduction strategy for a very long stretch (steps 74-163) without a decisive whole-strategy pivot, showing some sunk-cost persistence rather than systematic re-sequencing.
